text.title: Evolutionary Architecture Fitness Functions Decision Tree

decision-tree.root-question: What is under review: a single proposed fitness function, a function already running in CI, or the suite as a whole?

branch.question: Does the entry name one characteristic with a numeric metric and unit, a verbatim CI command, and a recorded baseline that passes the threshold today?

branch.conclusion: Rewrite the entry as one characteristic, one metric with a unit, or reject it.
Name the tool and the exact command; label `manual` only if no tool can measure it, and keep manual entries under one fifth of the suite.
Record the baseline and introduce the function in ratchet mode with a stated date for the absolute limit.
Classify it blocking or informational and triggered or continual; place holistic checks outside the pull-request path.

branch.question: How is it behaving: red or disabled across two reviews, slow enough that people skip it, green with no trend data, or healthy?

branch.conclusion: Reassign the owner and fix, re-baseline or delete the function at this review.
Move it to a scheduled or post-merge stage as a continual function; keep only atomic checks on pull requests.
Emit the measured value per run to a time series keyed by function id and commit before the next review.
No spec change needed; revisit at the declared review cadence.

branch.question: Does the suite include a structural function enforcing dependency direction and cycle-freedom with a named tool?

branch.conclusion: Add an ArchUnit / NetArchTest / dependency-cruiser / import-linter function with the allowed dependency graph written in the spec.
Run the cadence review against trend data; confirm every function still has a reachable owner.

example.p: Proposed function: "afferent coupling of `billing.core` below 12, measured by JDepend, current value 15". target == 'proposed_function', shape == 'fails_baseline' → conclusion r-ff-threshold-with-baseline-ratchet: ship as ratchet at 15, absolute limit 12 from next quarter.
